Let’s dive into Chapter 3: Turning Toward Each Other—The Power of Everyday Connection.
You know, beyond just showing appreciation or admiration, it’s really the small, everyday moments between partners that shape the quality of a marriage. These aren’t usually grand gestures. Instead, they’re tiny, often subtle bids for attention, affection, or support that pop up throughout the day.
Imagine this: your partner makes a comment about the weather, asks for a little help, or shares a funny story. Each of these is what we call a “bid”—an invitation to connect. Now, how you respond to these bids? That’s where the magic—or the trouble—happens.
There are three ways you might respond: turning toward, turning away, or turning against. Turning toward means you engage, even in a small way—maybe you make eye contact, smile, or just show some interest. Turning away is when you ignore or brush off the bid. And turning against? That’s when you respond with irritation or even hostility.
The impact of these responses really adds up. When partners make a habit of turning toward each other, even with the smallest gestures, they build up trust and intimacy. Over time, these moments create a real sense of partnership and security. But if you find yourselves often turning away or against, it can slowly lead to loneliness or resentment—even if everything looks fine on the surface.
Picture a couple at breakfast. One person mentions an interesting article in the newspaper, hoping to start a conversation. If the other responds with curiosity or just a simple nod, that little connection is reinforced. But if the comment is ignored—or worse, met with annoyance—a small chance for closeness slips away. Any single moment might seem like no big deal, but the pattern over weeks and months? That’s what shapes the emotional climate at home.
So, how can couples foster connection in these everyday moments? Here are a few simple habits:
Pay attention to those little bids and respond with genuine interest or affection. Make time for shared rituals—like meals together, evening walks, or just those bedtime chats. And don’t forget, your tone and body language often say more than your words.
The real secret isn’t about grand romantic gestures. It’s about being present and attentive in the ordinary, day-to-day moments. When you make turning toward each other a habit, you build a sense of “us-ness”—that feeling of being a team, something bigger than just two individuals.
Of course, life gets busy. Stress and hectic schedules can make it harder to notice or respond to these bids. That’s why, during those crazy times, it’s even more important to be intentional. Even a brief moment—a touch on the arm, a shared smile—can mean a lot.
Over time, this practice becomes self-reinforcing. As trust and intimacy grow, it feels safer to make bids, and you become more confident that your needs will be met. It’s like a positive feedback loop—connection leads to more connection.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the strength of a marriage isn’t just about how you handle the big stuff. It’s really about how you navigate those small, everyday moments. By turning toward each other, you build a strong, resilient bond—one that can weather whatever life throws your way.
